purpose: Terazosin is used to treat two main conditions: high blood pressure and an enlarged prostate gland (called BPH). If you have BPH, it helps relieve symptoms like difficulty urinating, weak urine flow, or needing to urinate frequently. When used for blood pressure, it helps lower it to a safer level and reduce your risk of heart attack or stroke.
how_it_works: Terazosin works by relaxing the muscles in your blood vessels and in the prostate gland. Think of it like loosening a tight grip — when those muscles relax, blood can flow more easily through your vessels, which lowers blood pressure. For the prostate, relaxing those muscles makes it easier for urine to flow out of your bladder.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when you stand up quickly. Headache, tiredness or feeling weak. Stuffy or runny nose. Swelling in your hands or feet. Some men may notice a decrease in semen during orgasm, which is harmless.
warnings: This medicine can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure when you stand up, especially after your very first dose or if you miss doses — this can make you feel faint or dizzy, so be careful when getting up from a bed or chair. Take your first dose at bedtime to reduce this risk. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you are scheduled for cataract eye surgery, as this medication can cause a complication called 'floppy iris syndrome.' Tell all your doctors and dentist you take this medicine.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 1 mg taken at bedtime. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose over several weeks depending on how you respond. The typical maintenance dose ranges from 1 mg to 10 mg once daily. Always take it at the same time each day, and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
